title: Parent-child (small-to-big) retrieval
summary: Match the query against small child chunks for precision, then return the larger parent section, page or window to the model for context.
useIf: Small chunks find the answer but the model needs the surrounding section to use it.
avoidIf: Retrieval must be a single cheap lookup with a tiny prompt, or documents are so short that a single chunk size already works.

explain.md: **Parent-child** (also called small-to-big) separates the two roles of a chunk. **Children** are small (a sentence, a paragraph or about 128 to 256 tokens) and are the only things embedded, so matching is sharp. A **parent** is the larger unit the child came from: a section, a page or a window of neighbours. At query time the retriever finds the best children, looks up their parents, removes duplicates and sends the parents to the model.

explain.title: Small-to-big retrieval
explain.alt: A query searches the child chunk index. Top children are grouped by parent id and duplicates are removed. The parents are fetched and sent to the model.
explain.src:
flowchart LR
  Q["Query"] --> S["Search child chunks"]
  S --> G["Group by parent id"]
  G --> D["Dedupe and rank parents"]
  D --> P["Fetch parent text"]
  P --> M["Model"]

explain.md: There are three common shapes. **Parent lookup** returns the whole section or page. **Window expansion** returns the matched chunk plus the neighbours before and after it, using the ordinal position (the Text Split skill outputs `ordinalPositions` and offsets [[tr2]]). **Auto-merging** replaces several matched siblings with their parent when enough of them match; LlamaIndex's `AutoMergingRetriever` does this with a threshold [[tr40]].

In Azure AI Search you build the parent-child shape with **index projections**, which write several child documents from one parent in a skillset. The child index needs a key and a `parent_id`-style field that is `Edm.String` and `filterable` and not the document key. `projectionMode` is `skipIndexingParentDocuments` (recommended, uniform documents) or `includeIndexingParentDocuments` (the default). Projected keys contain a random hash that changes when the parent changes, so stale children are replaced. Children of a deleted parent are removed only if the data source has a deletion detection policy [[tr4]].

You can afford a parent lookup or extra storage
Parents have stable ids and clear boundaries

pitfalls.symptom: The prompt fills with the same section three times
pitfalls.cause: Several children from one parent were each expanded
pitfalls.fix: Group by parent id, return each parent once and rank by its best child

pitfalls.symptom: Answers quote outdated text after a document update
pitfalls.cause: Child vectors were refreshed but copied parent text was not
pitfalls.fix: Rewrite all children of a changed parent, or fetch parent text by id at query time

pitfalls.symptom: Stale child chunks remain after a source file is deleted
pitfalls.cause: In AI Search, child removal requires a deletion detection policy on the data source
pitfalls.fix: Define the policy from the first run and reconcile child counts against the source

pitfalls.symptom: A user sees text from a section they cannot access
pitfalls.cause: The parent carries different permissions than the matched child
pitfalls.fix: Copy access fields to parents and children at ingest and filter before expansion

scenarios.title: Clause lookup in long contracts
scenarios.situation: Lawyers search 200-page contracts. A matching clause is only meaningful with its definitions and exceptions in the same section. Answers can use larger prompts.
unknowns: How long is a typical section?
How often do contracts change after indexing?
scenarios.question: Which retrieval design fits?

options.name: Embed clause-sized children, return the parent section, dedupe by parent
options.why: Clause matching stays sharp and the model gets definitions and exceptions.
options.tradeoff: A second lookup or larger index, and bigger prompts.

options.name: Embed whole sections only
options.tradeoff: Vectors blur across clauses, so exact clause lookup is weaker.

options.name: Embed single sentences and return only them
options.why: Sentences without their section lose definitions and exceptions.
options.tradeoff: Right for corpora of independent, self-contained statements.

flips.then: Return a window around the match instead of the whole section.
Fetch parent text by id so only children need re-embedding.

scenarios.takeaway: Match small, answer big, and decide where the parent lives.

scenarios.title: Chat assistant on a hard latency limit
scenarios.situation: A voice assistant must retrieve in a single index call and keep prompts short. The corpus is modest and storage is plentiful.
unknowns: How wide must the context be?
scenarios.question: What do you build?

options.name: Parent-child with the parent text stored on each child document
options.why: Sharp child match and the parent arrives in the same call, with storage as the price.
options.tradeoff: Updating a parent means rewriting all its children, and the index grows.

options.name: Single-level chunks of about 512 tokens
options.why: Simplest design inside the latency limit.
options.tradeoff: One size must serve both matching and context.

options.name: Parent-child with a separate parent store and a second lookup
options.why: The extra round trip breaks the single-call latency limit.
options.tradeoff: Right when storage is tight and a second call fits the budget.

flips.then: Prefer single-level chunks to avoid rewriting copied parents.
A separate parent store saves storage and eases updates.

scenarios.takeaway: Where the parent lives is a latency and storage decision, and also a data model choice.

quiz.q: In parent-child retrieval, what is embedded and what is sent to the model?
options: The parent is embedded and the child is sent
Both are embedded and only the child is sent
Neither is embedded, the parent is summarised
The children are embedded and the parent (or window) is sent
quiz.explain: Children give sharp matching, parents give context. Embedding the parent defeats the purpose, and sending only the child loses the context you wanted.

quiz.q: Which AI Search index projection settings or rules are true?
options: The parent id field must be `Edm.String` and filterable
The parent id field must be the document key
Child chunks of a deleted parent are always removed automatically
quiz.explain: The parent id field is a filterable string and not the key. Skipping parent documents gives a uniform index shape. Children of a deleted parent are removed only when the data source has a deletion detection policy.

quiz.q: Top results show the same section repeated three times and the prompt overflows. What is the fix?
options: Group matches by parent id and return each parent once
quiz.explain: Several children from one parent each expanded to the same parent. Grouping and ranking by parent removes duplicates. Search parameters, dimensions and overlap do not affect expansion duplicates.

flashcards.back: Embed small child chunks for precise matching, then return the larger parent (section, page or window) to the model for context.

flashcards.front: What must the parent id field be in an AI Search index projection?
flashcards.back: An `Edm.String` field marked `filterable`, and not the document key.

flashcards.front: What does the LlamaIndex AutoMergingRetriever do?
flashcards.back: It merges matched sibling leaf nodes into their parent when enough of them match a set threshold.

flashcards.front: When are children of a deleted parent removed in AI Search?
flashcards.back: Only when the data source has a deletion detection policy. Without it, stale children remain.
